tips.comment: Third at Chepstow and second at Goodwood in the last two runs. I do think there is going to be another better run from Al Khawaneej River. The distance is the same as the runner-up finish in Goodwood, and I think this will be a win around Sandown.

Calvert has improved for the recent two runs at this distance to be second. Ran over CD a class lower last time and rallied late but just lost. May have won in more experienced hands, which he gets here in the shape of Jim Crowley. Curragh came back to form last time and looks like he could make a good race of it.
Finished last time out on a distance that didn't suit, eased over a furlong out. Has won over the trip previously. Down in grade but up in price from previous shorter prices!
Curran is proven at the distance, handles all ground, and ran a career-best when just denied last time. Well treated off this mark and primed to strike for an in-form yard.

Red Flyer is in stall number 2, which is decent for his stalking style with a steady pace that I expect today. That should suit him well. He ran a solid race at Newmarket last time, finishing third off 75, showing me that he handles distances from 14 furlongs to 2 miles and prefers firm ground. With a consistent record and on a very fair mark of 74, he has 3 wins and 7 places from 18 runs at this class. David Egan rides again for Kevin Jewell. Looks an each-way chance with a decent shout at the win if he gets his preferred conditions here.

Moel Arthur steps up markedly in trip to 1m6f and looks well worth chancing at this price. He shaped with more promise than the bare result suggested when fifth over 1m2f at Sandown last time, staying on steadily in a race not really suited to him. The extra distance here should unlock further improvement for a horse who's bred to stay well and has shown hints of stamina previously.
Similar runs the last twice, meeting trouble in running and conceding first runs to subsequent winners. Down in grade from last time, should take advantage of that here.

Phoenix Of Spain sired a grey gelding who could be enjoying the ground conditions being good. The four-year-old has been dropped a pound to 81 from the last two outings and three pounds lower than the previous two. Aidan Keeley has the ride for Roger Varien, whose charge could be having a going forward night here.
Orbaan is holding form well, suited by the mile trip and a sound surface. Consistent in this grade, narrowly beaten last time, and looks poised to strike off a workable mark.

Preference here goes to the Peter Chapple-Hyam runner, Desperate Dan. Arrives with plenty to prove after being dealt quite a tough hand on his seasonal return. Not ideally placed and quite surprised this horse was not taken out due to the ground riding quicker than ideal. This seems a more realistic aim dropping down into a C4 grade. All his best form is on heavy, which leaves doubts, but he's very effective over this trip and his comfortable win at Nottingham by five lengths certainly makes him worth exploring, if by chance, he can be effective on good.

Pearl Eye lines up at Sandown looking well-treated off a mark of 81, having previously won a strong Class 2 at Doncaster earlier this season. He shaped better than the bare result when last seen at Ascot, racing prominently in a competitive handicap before fading late. The return to a mile or more on a galloping track suits, and with Neil Callan booked, he looks set for a bold run.
Went close last time out at Haydock over tonight's distance. Running off the same mark tonight looks well treated. Tonight should be fine and should be hard to beat.

Gelded son of Soldier's Call & Warm Welcome ( Dam's sire Motivator ) who was last seen winning at Haydock 22 days ago getting the better of a tightly bunched battle at the finish the handicapper has reacted with a 4lb rise and Captain Harry is now operating on a mark of 71 however a 4lb rise is not likely to prevent this improving individual from getting the better of things yet again here as he still looks to be a step ahead of accesor here in my point of view and having found himself another suitable looking assignment here Andrew Balding's inmate can play a huge role in this class 5 handicap over on the business end expect to see Captain Harry thundering home with jockey Rob Hornby taking the ride merits serious consideration here
Was returning from a 7-month absence when a close-up 2nd over 7f at Newbury, which was a much-improved effort. Should strip fitter now and is expected to go close.

PRINCESS AMBER has been placed in two races from five starts. She finished third over 7f at Ffos Las on her latest outing last month. The course, distance, and going should suit her. She seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Going to take a gamble on this one today. Turpin is in stall number 5, which should give him a decent position early on with a steady pace expected. He is coming off a break after a wind operation and has shown modest form in handicaps. His best run was over 7 furlongs on the AW. Marked at 63, his progress here in handicaps remains to be seen, but David Egan rides for James Boyle, who may help. He does need a big step forward to be competitive here, so small stakes.

Silver Arrow is a little interesting. Makes second start for Lemos De Souza yard here. Ran some nice races at age two for Amy Murphy yard, culminating in a win over seven furlongs at Chelmsford. Didn't look ready for return to action a month ago (ran keenly) and could be better prepared on second seasonal start. Dark Angel grey, still a bit unexposed.
Made all last time out and faded over the closing furlongs. Drop in trip and a tongue strap may work the oracle. Good each way chance.
Favourite looks the place to go here. Ran well in 4th in the same grade as today, only 1 pound extra to carry and up in distance. Chances.

The Simon and Ed Crisford yard have finally turned the corner and are hitting form at present and War Supremo delivered last time out after showing a lot of promise. With Kieran Shoemark aboard he should manage the 4lb rise.
Been running in listed company the previous two races. Eased down on last start and pressed the leader on the penultimate. In lower company, may have a chance.

Suffering from seconditis this month but hoping Neardown can change that tomorrow. He did start his career by winning his debut run at Chester last August. Made handicap debut LTO when 5 of 7 last month and hoping now with dropped mark he can improve.

Needed run on reappearance run last time, his first for 10 months. He was 2nd in his maiden around here over 7f just over a year ago. That was a decent race, and several finishing behind him that day are running off significantly higher marks than 77, which is what he is making his handicap debut off today.

Roach Power was off a reduced mark at Ffos Las last week and won a five furlongs handicap. Four wins so far for the Irish horse who is sporting blinkers tonight. I do think Roach Power will go off favourite and win.

Connies Rose is in stall number 4 which is fine for her usual forward-going style and the pace looks good enough to suit her. She has an excellent course and distance record with 4 wins from 10 runs and a 40% strike rate, and her overall record over 6f is solid. She ran respectably here last time when rushed up early in a visor and now reverts to tongue strap and cheekpieces which she has previously won in. Her current mark of 67 is very workable and George Harris has her in consistent form. She is a Chepstow regular and has a great chance today
A decent-looking claimer takes most of the penalty off for Scenario, so I think this is a viable bet for the double up. Should be difficult to beat as clearly bang in form.
I'll chance TIME AFTER TIME in a forecast with the favorite here. Just seems to be coming into some semblance of form and might be capable of landing something like this soon.

He's a four time course winner who took this exact race last year and showed signs of a return to form with a close fourth at Bath last time out. He clearly thrives at Chepstow and looks well-suited to conditions again tonight. With pace to aim at and proven track record, he rates a live contender at generous odds.

The lowest grade and the oldest runner in the race. Even so, he is the top-rated horse in the field and always runs his race. He won on the sand in February off a higher mark, so assuming he handles the undulations, he looks good in the context of this race.

I'd have been a lot happier if this was a handicap race, and it might be worth noting what she does here today. Nothing really to note on the 3 runs, and the opening mark confirms that, but she has had a wind operation since that last run 3 months ago and is up in trip here today. There's every chance they're just using this race as a tester for a number of reasons, so a small wager is advised.

This classified race is full of the usual dodgepots, and despite there being 15 runners, it looks highly likely to go to an unexposed horse such as this one rather than one of the more exposed ones whose limited abilities we are already aware of. The key for me is this horse's 2nd in her only run over this C&D. She has only had 5 starts, and that was easily the best. It actually is very easy to make a case for that form being good enough to win this since the horses around her were around a 55-rated average, and that's definitely good enough to win this. The first-time visor might also bring about further improvement, and the 22/1 looks excellent value.

Won a class 6 here eight days ago over 1.2 miles, but is a C/D winner so drop back to this mile not an issue and 4lb penalty may not stop them, as they do have solid form @ this class 5 level. Good jockey up who does well for this stable and shrewd trainer duo who like to have winners @ one of their local tracks, are 21 percent with an impressive 69.88 on their 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 8/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Good chance here, stepping down a little bit after finishing half a length behind Ianna. Good form and 5 pounds better off in weight.

Darvel drops back in grade here following a decent effort at Sandown. He is a course and distance winner in the past, which, as we well know, is a significant advantage here. Patrick Chamings saddled a winner at Salisbury on Wednesday, and can follow up with Darvel.

Looks too big a price to be ignored today. A course and distance winner. In decent form and a capable apprentice taking off five pounds, bringing the rating to 55, which is good enough to win off. Worth a shot.

The race looks wide open, and it's possible that the mare can add to her sole career success at Leopardstown in 2023. She hasn't threatened in any of her races this year but traveled well into her last race before finding zilch off the bridle. On the basis that she probably needed that run after a three and a half months break, she looks a sporting each-way bet off a career-low mark.

Most Wanted lines up here with a solid chance, coming off a convincing 4-length win at Leicester where he made all the running. He's up in the weights for that effort but remains competitively treated, all things considered. If he can dictate the pace again, he has every chance of repeating the feat. He offers value as a front-runner with proven form and is worth a bet at this price.

Was well beaten over today's trip at Ffos Las at the end of last month but improved to finish a close second (by a neck) over the same track and trip nine days ago. Is a two time course winner over 1m. Should be thereabouts.
Drops in grade after racing over this trip in a Class 5 last month and was a decent runner-up in this Class 6 grade at Lingfield on penultimate start off a pound higher and also over this trip.

Course winner who has not been beaten that far in their 3 runs this term and has dropped to a very attractive mark of 48 here. Good apprentice back up claiming 3lb and shrewd trainer is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 20 percent, making current 8/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Fighting Queen is in stall number 5, which is fine as she is quite versatile with the draw numbers, and the pace should be fair for her running style. She won well at Bath two starts ago off 55, showing me lots of ability and handled firm conditions well that day also. Last time, she got no run when needed and was eased late, so that effort can be forgiven. Her current mark of 57 is still very workable, and this is her class level. She stays at least a mile strongly, and with a clearer trip, she has every chance today.

Just three career runs for the 3-year-old filly. Beaten just a neck over 10 furlongs on her second start in a Listed contest, the form given a big boost by the winner since. She wasn’t disgraced in the Group 1 Oaks last time out over 12 furlongs. Back down in trip will suit her tonight and she should be a big player back at this Listed level.
Placed at Listed level last year and won a Class 2 handicap over a mile here in May. Stays this trip, has won here, and is more than capable of winning in this class.
Ran in listed, 5 pounds better off here after a very good run just behind Qilin Queen. Should come on again and be able to get in the frame.

Talented filly completed a 4-timer when battling to a narrow success over 10 furlongs at Lingfield in January. Handicap mark went up 18 lbs as a result of those wins. Placed in a Group 3 at Newcastle over 10 furlongs last month. Found the drop to a mile too sharp at Pontefract last time and will appreciate the step back up in trip.

Imperial Quarter is in stall number 3, which is ideal, and the race should be run at a good pace, which suits her hold-up style. She has placed in Listed company last time at Pontefract despite a slow start, beaten just over five lengths in a solid field. Yet to win in this class or on similar going, but has placed a couple of times in both scenarios. Current mark of 99 looks doable based on what she has achieved so far, and she is lightly raced and trained by Roger Varian with Callum Rodriguez booked. Could sneak in here if things fall right today.
The ground will not be as quick as last time when he disappointed over a mile. He will appreciate this step up to 10f and is worth an each-way bet.
Ran a little flat last time after a two-month break. However, up in trip, listed event, Billy the Whizz in the saddle needs to improve but is a decent price to do so.

A decent reappearance run when second over a mile at Nottingham last time out. Will appreciate the step back up in trip to 10 furlongs. Slightly juicy good ground is a bonus too. Yard in good form and goes well both at York and in this race.

Going to have a small ew on this one who we know will be fine on todays going and distance. 4th twice in last two losted races and with the exeption of a couple maybe three, there are question marks on most at a lot shorter odds than this one, so worth the small ew imo.
VICARIO has won a race at 6f. Fifth in a Listed race over 1m at Pontefract on her latest outing earlier this month. Upped in trip to 1m 2f should suit and could well be able to win this race.

The 3yo filly is looking very progressive. She has won 4 of her last 5 races. She was a nice 2L winner three weeks ago, never in trouble when making the running and she hit the line strong. She earned a huge RPR rating that day. Her progress might not be finished yet and she now has Oisin Murphy taking over in the saddle.

Lady Roxby looks a very big price here given the manner of her win at Beverley last time. She showed she had improved markedly from her two-year-old form when second on seasonal debut at Thirsk. Then came that very impressive win last time, and the form has been franked by the runner-up since then. Michael Herrington is a very underrated trainer, which tends to see some of his runners going off at bigger prices than they should be.
Top Juggler is lightly raced, consistent on good ground, and narrowly denied last time. Proven in this class, handles the conditions well, and remains well-treated off 76. Likely to contend.

With only two outings this year so far Diomed Duke may still have a bit more in reserve. Jockey and trainer in form and a good draw in the race helps as well. Not too sure about the weight carried today but the wonderful Dakota Gold won this off ten stones! Worth a shot at this price due to a very strong favourite in the race.

Having finished in the top positions in 4 of her last 5 races, she secured 2nd place in a handicap at Thirsk just 10 days ago, where she was held up until the final furlong. With the visor on once more, this could be a favourable race for this distance winner. This reliable contender certainly deserves consideration for an each-way bet at 12/1.
Ew interest for 5 places with bits and pieces for it. Ran well enough on penultimate start over course and distance, getting no luck in running and is 3lb lower here.

Im Next is in stall number 16, which is far from ideal given the track bias and early pace dynamics. Though the overall pace is expected to be good, which could help him settle. This progressive 3-year-old has won twice over this trip from seven attempts and ran well in a higher-grade contest last time, finishing third after going too hard early. His current mark of 75 looks very fair based on that Newcastle win, and he has placed at this rating already. Danny Allan keeps the ride for Tim Easterby, and while the draw is a worry to me, his consistency and form make him a solid each-way chance with a shot at the win here.

Al Hussar, a 3-year-old gelding, ran poorly last time but was bumped leaving the stalls. So, he is better judged on his previous race when he was 4th of 7, beaten less than a length. Down 2 more pounds in the handicap for his latest effort.
They are stepping this one up in trip slightly with the same jockey on board. Worth a small each-way saver bet for the 5 places available.
Great price again, especially each way. Been running well enough all season, and another 3rd would be a great return here. Can win.

Thecla comes into this one after a warm-up run early in the month after a break. Speculative, but she looked okay with a win back last September followed with a fourth from ten. Price and five places, so an each-way go.

Should really avoid big field sprint handicaps as they are total lotteries, but when you fancy one, you fancy one. Sugar Baby was an eye-catching 5th of 18 over course and distance 13 days ago (beaten less than 2 lengths) and would have finished closer still when short of room in the last half furlong. Aiden Brookes rides again and off the same mark looks great each way value with 6 places on offer with 365 & Skybet.

Progressive type who won a similar event over course and distance in May. Best effort since came when losing nothing in defeat to a well-handicapped Aberama Gold in another big field here a fortnight ago. Something similar should see him bang there once again this evening.

Although there are 22 runners for this class 4 handicap, it may not be as competitive as the numbers suggest. Winged Messenger is of interest. A four-year-old who is in good form at the moment, combined with a strong draw and a very good pilot aboard. Should run well.

After good runs at Newcastle and York, it was an underwhelming performance last time when well off the pace at Doncaster. That was over 7f and in firm ground and should be better suited to return to 6f and good to soft. Each way chance at 12/1.

Race 4 at York today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,207 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Noble Consort from the Julie Camacho yard, and will be ridden by Ryan Sexton. This son of Too Darn Hot is holding some serious form recently with two 2nds and four wins in his last 6 races. Must have some chance in this field and warrants consideration.

Liam Bailey's Dicko The Legend won this race twelve months ago off just a lb lower mark than the one of 68 he carries here. The five-year-old has been drawn in the same low stall three he started from last year and has recently undergone wind surgery. 22/1 looks a huge price, and with six places being paid, he looks a fantastic each-way bet to me.

Showtime Mahomes took a while to find his form this season. The yard was struggling in the early part of the year, which explains that. He won at Carlisle last time and could defy the penalty, given he had come down a few pounds prior to that run. He looks to be drawn in the right part of the track, which will help his chances.

Unexposed 4yo, with 2 wins from 8 starts. Three runs this year and he ran a nice race at this track two weeks ago, beaten around a length in a 16 runner handicap. He was drawn widest on the far side and held up, most of the action came centre and near side. Plenty to like how he finished the race off. A slightly lower mark tonight and the extra furlong can help his chances.

Third in this race last year off this same rating of OR70. Has maintained her form. Ten wins from 69 career starts (something of a Hamilton specialist). Ran fairly well a couple of weeks ago though wide of the main field. A bit of cut in the ground might help a lot, especially with high draw in stall 21. A well handicapped possible winner in a field of plenty of contenders.

These are very big odds as he has not been disgraced in any races recently actually going quite close on occasions.
Was rated higher for his previous yard so today's mark looks workable and this step up to 6f looks ideal.
Bang in form stable and this one looks the pick of the three they have in this race based on jockey bookings.
Huge price here to make the frame. Always out of the picture recently, but will win at a big price very, very soon.

The 8yo has had a nice 9 months off the track to freshen up and get his act together after some below par efforts last year. He has good stats when returning from a break. The yard has had five winners in the last two weeks for a 21% strike rate. He has been racing off a way higher mark in the last three seasons and could be worth an EW shout.

Finished a lowly 15th of 16 last time out 14 days ago on a same as today class 4 over 5f on fast going and 81 rating. An easier surface today will suit with rating down to 78 and usual jockey on board.
Bit of a punt on last year's form - two wins and a few other useful runs - but hasn't done much this year and needs to improve here.

Hasn't won for almost eighteen months and mark has been steadily dropping. Has now reached a level where he can be competitive as shown on his last outing when he finished a close fourth at Down Royal.
Course and distance winner. Won fifteen runner at Naas fifteen days ago last time out. On the up and could be the answer.

A typically competitive Cork Sprint Handicap in which, although still a maiden, Lismacbryan Hill looks interesting. This will be her 14th start, and although unplaced in all 6 starts last year, she has been placed in 3 of her last 6 this season. Her best run was probably when 3rd of 27 in a 6-furlong Curragh handicap in May, while last time she was again 3rd at Bellewstown earlier this month over 5 furlongs. Back at 6 furlongs off a 1lb lower mark, she looks like a good EW bet with 6 places on offer.

This maiden has been close in 3 starts this season, including a solid 4th in a handicap at Navan 12 days ago. She could be a contender if the cheekpieces are effective. The 11/1 odds are particularly appealing with extra places on the table.

Lakota Lady is a 5-year-old mare trained by Michael J Browne. She has shown some zest in her last two starts. She finished 5/15 on her penultimate start but had the wrong side of the draw, finishing 1/5 in her group. Last time out, she was beaten only 2 lengths despite not getting the clearest of runs and was hampered at the start. She was nearest at the finish. She runs off a lowly 8st 13lb and bottom weight and is stepped back up to 6f, which should suit her under a notable jockey booking in Seammie Heffernan, who replaces an apprentice who has ridden Lakota Lady the last two times.
Faded alarmingly when made favourite at Limerick earlier this month but ZARAGOZA had shown decent form prior and is readily given another chance dropped back slightly in trip.
Has not been in the best of form and, as a result, has come down in the weights. This is a wide-open race, and I feel JB could be ready to start competing again.
Should give a good go in a massive field. 6 places on offer. If getting the run through, should give this a chance. 3 lengths off last time but better off in weights.
Upped in trip today after a promising effort over 5 furlongs last time. Can run a place if getting away better. First-time blinkers could be the answer.

Being the stubborn sod that I am I tend to approach these type of handicaps at Cork in a certain way & that being look for something A] Drawn Wide (if the ground is quick) B] something light as a feather & C] something different being tried so with that being said I've landed on Kevin Smith's 9 year old Gelding BLUE WOOD now Im sure he won't have many supporters but I feel like this Son of REQUINTO's last run can have a line put right through it, it was too far. Now prior to last time outs run we've had 7f runs where this charge has been there (or there abouts) 1f out but has been headed so in theory the drop to 6f doesn't look the craziest of ideas & now runs off his last winning mark & what's interesting is this lads only attempt over this trip on fast ground produced a 3rd ¾ finish (off a mark of 56). Jockey Wesley Joyce seems to know how to get a tune from this lad. 6 places, decent odds - I'm in.

Appointed a mark of 60 in its handicap debut here, Sandi O Mali, ridden by Nicola Burns who can claim another 7lb here, has been out the traps rapid but gets collared late on. So this 5f trip might just be exploited against some exposed ones.

This is a trainer's only entry. He's got out today as they are reapplying the cheekpieces, and they have got a 5 lbs claiming jockey booking/change. Worth a small each way saver bet for the 6 places available.

Nordic Passage has left betting stable of JF Levins and joined little known outfit of Maurice Ahern. Career record of six wins from 57 starts. Handicap mark has dropped a long way in very short time (OR79 two years ago down to OR42 here). Ten years old now. Drawn in stall 19. Rory Cleary rides. Would have a big shout if retaining some of his former ability.

A seven-race maiden, she looked unlucky two starts ago at Ballinrobe when having anything but a trouble-free run at crucial times in the race. That was in an extended 9f maiden but has run no sort of race back in handicaps on her last three starts. She has a bit to prove on the back of those efforts but can go close from a falling mark if bouncing back.

I was following this one and gave up on it, but i'm going to give it another chance today for a couple of reasons. Mark has dropped down alot this year and they are trying cheek pieces again, which they used a few times at the end of last year, but were not used in both races this year. Gets a good claiming jockey change as well and imo seems to run better when around 9 stone (9-4 today with claim) so with a bit of luck, could nick a place. Some other ex tracker's American In Paris (decent chance) and Lorrs Girl which always looks a tricky ride, but i've seen glimpses.
Nancy J ran very well at Ascot last time and might find this race a lot easier. The small field might also help here, and the yard seems to be among the winners again, so plenty of positives here.
This could be a very tight race between Sonaro, Nancy J, and Mojave's River, who comes from the stable that won this last year. It could win again.
Unexposed horse in the race, could be anything and looks set to improve. Should put it up to the more experienced runners in the field.
Reiki Revolution is a previous winner of a bumper and ran a fine race at Cork two weeks ago when runner-up and beaten by less than a length there. That is clearly the best recent form on offer.
Has shown some fair form in four novice hurdles at around this sort of trip so far. With first-time blinkers now applied, it looks to have been found a decent opportunity to get off the mark.

Reiki Revolution and William Butler have the best form but they have also both had plenty of chances so the Willie Mullins trained NORTH MOON gets a confident vote despite a disappointing bumper effort.

Midnight Moonshine is a 6-year-old gelding trained by William Harvey. He is 0-5 under rules, rated 100 over fences, and showed promise on his hurdling debut latest. He should go well again as he was clearly fancied last time out, moving from 5-1 into 7-2, and should appreciate today's step up in trip as he did all his good work late on when beaten just a length behind Jazz De Cotte.
The stable is in form, and the selection had excuses last time, jumping poorly and returning with cuts. If Henry can get her jumping sorted, there is a winner in waiting here.
Trappy race and siding with the Willie Mullins horse here. Should give a good go after going off odds-on favorite and disappointing last time out.

This selection's best effort to date was a 2nd place finish over the distance of 20.5 furlongs. Racing around 20 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful the ground will suit. Mark Walsh is retained. Hopeful it can go close.

Bocelli's Voice is a 9-year-old gelding trained by Dermot A McLoughlin. He is relatively unexposed as a chaser and has been rated as high as 121. He ran well this time last year when finishing runner-up at Wexford, beaten just 3 lengths. He runs today off a career-low handicap mark of 103 with Patrick M O'Brien's 7lb conditional claim and could be one to consider now dropped down to a more suitable trip.
Past course and distance winner and won here on good ground back in April. Has run in better class races last twice but a consistent type back in a grade that best suits.
The AJ Martin-trained Movie King has been running on the flat but can get involved at a price here back over fences where he has performed well before.

This selection's best effort to date was a 4th place finish over the distance of 23.5 furlongs. It drops back down to race around 20 furlongs in today's contest. Hopeful the ground will suit. Jack Kennedy is in the saddle. Hopeful it can go close.

Robin Des Roost is a 15-year-old veteran, well beaten in both starts this season. Blinkers need to transform back in trip. This four-time chase winner over distances in and around today's trip handles the ground. Last win came off a mark of 77, winning quite comfortably from 10lb out of the handicap at Downpatrick in June 24. Interesting that he wore a first-time tongue tie that day and could rebound today with conditions to suit under the useful Darragh O'Keefe.

Looks like a two-horse race, and this one is well in from a second last time out. That was its best run to date. Any running to that form, and he wins this. Can be yet another winner from the shrewd Slattery outfit.

A race full to the brim with inconsistent sorts but the very well bred AMAVASYA did look as though she might appreciate this sort of test when doing her best work close home last time out over 1m 1f and gets a tentative vote.

Vervain is in stall number 4, which suits her front-running style, and the pace looks steady enough to help her get a good tow into the race. She ran to form last time over 10 at Naas, finishing third, and that shows me she can handle this step up in trip. Although inconsistent overall and still a maiden, her mark of 55 is extremely fair, and she’s in the hands of an in-form Joseph Murphy, with Gavin Carroll riding again. She could sneak a place if she repeats that latest effort and gets a smooth run, or even better, the win.

Oranzona is a 3-year-old filly trained by Ms. Sheila Lavery. She has yet to win in four starts and was beaten 9 lengths in sixth at Killarney on her handicap debut. It's unlikely she will reverse form with What's New, but it's early days. Today's trip and further should bring the best out of her in time, being a half-sister to Annecheriea, a four-time winner over 2 miles with Lavery and today's owners, winning off marks of 62, 68, and 55. Today's current handicap mark of 55 for Oranzona should be taken into consideration on her second start in a handicap. She's turned out quickly after just 11 days under Donagh O'Connor, his only ride of the day in the lucky last.
Decent third at Down Royal last time and has been placed in listed company previously. Has enough ability to take this.
Promising debut 2 weeks ago when finishing well, only to be hampered when getting going. Up in trip today, which looks ideal. Good draw and from a top in-form stable.

An open-looking handicap where Amanirenas has dropped to a very attractive mark and looks great each-way value at 20/1 with 5 places up for grabs. He ran well last time at Bellestown despite losing ground out wide. This drop back in trip looks a big plus.
